svg.title: Test layers for Cedar's plug-ins
svg.desc: Four layers from bottom to top. Layer 1, pure rule tests: 50 tests of classes without Dataverse types, run on any operating system in milliseconds on every commit; they prove the business decisions. Layer 2, component tests with fakes: 10 tests that run a real plug-in class against a fake service provider, fake execution context and an in-memory fake Organization service on .NET Framework on Windows; they prove the wiring: which stage and message, images, identity used for each call, number and shape of data calls, outputs and exceptions. Layer 3, deployed checks in Cedar-Dev and Cedar-Test: the request files, trace logs and the registration compared with the manifest; they prove registration, security and real platform behaviour. Layer 4, user acceptance in Cedar-Test with test personas. A side note lists what no fake can prove: security roles, filtering attributes, real query results, transactions and other publishers' steps.
svg.text: What each test layer proves (cheapest and most numerous at the bottom)

1. Pure rule tests: 50 tests, any OS, milliseconds, every commit
DispatchReadiness, ArrivalRules, KeyVaultRules: no Dataverse types.
Proves: every business decision and every message text.
Rule of thumb: a failing test in layer 1 costs seconds to find, in layer 2 a minute, in layer 3 an hour, and a failure found by a customer costs a day and trust.
Push every check as far down as it can honestly go, and no further.
